subject: Configurations in which session$request$PATH_INFO has a value (other than just "/websocket/")?

messages.author: a5edeb4fa89b826c
messages.subject: Configurations in which session$request$PATH_INFO has a value (other than just "/websocket/")?
parts:
So, I was thinking of potentially using session$request$PATH_INFO in a Shiny app in a way similar to how it can be used in a traditional CGI script.
(See http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3875#section-4.1.5 for the definition of PATH_INFO that I have in mind.)

However, I'm wondering about the configurations in which session$request$PATH_INFO will actually be set (to something other than "/websocket/").  I'm particularly interested in configurations involving running Shiny Server behind a reverse proxy, such as nginx or Apache, but am also curious about any other configurations in which PATH_INFO gets set.  (e.g. Could it be set when running a Shiny app directly from RStudio via runApp(), for example?)

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Configurations in which session$request$PATH_INFO has a value (other than just "/websocket/")?
parts:
It's not particularly interesting, because session$request is always the request that initiates the websocket session (i.e. initiated by JavaScript). I'm guessing URL params might be more interesting to you?
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/client-data.html

messages.subject: Re: Configurations in which session$request$PATH_INFO has a value (other than just "/websocket/")?
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply Joe.  And, yes, I'll definitely be using URL params now that you've clarified for me that session$request will only ever represent the websocket connection.  I was thinking the PATH_INFO-styled URLs might have had a slightly "cleaner" look in this app and maybe be less susceptible to truncation when users copy and paste them and stuff like that, but that's subjective and a very minor consideration.  An URL param (just one in this case) will work well too.

Thanks again!

Joel
